_rule: ARC-07-S07. THE list of cloud-sync paths, satisfied by three implementations: the server's detectCloudSync() in src/store/paths.ts, the bootstrap's stdlib re-implementation in tools/snowarch/lib/cloud-sync.mjs (ARC-06-S05, for a checkout that has never run npm ci), and the doctor's E-25 (ARC-08-S03). Three tables that merely look alike would drift; one fixture cannot.
_shape: synced[]: { path, provider, root, why } — every one of these MUST be detected, with that provider. quiet[]: { path, why } — every one of these MUST be null. env[]: { path, set: {VAR: value}, provider, root, why } — the Windows environment roots, which no path pattern can catch.
_paths: Synthetic. No path here exists on any machine, and none is derived from a real user's home directory.

synced.why: AC 3. macOS mounts every vendor under ~/Library/CloudStorage/<Provider>-<tenant>.
AC 3. How macOS spells iCloud on disk, and no user calls it that.
AC 3. The tenant is suffixed onto the folder name with a spaced hyphen.
AC 3. The outer folder matches first.
A vendor the table does not name is still synchronised; the honest answer names the mount.
ARC-04-S02 criterion 8, kept: the plain consumer folder.
ARC-06-S05's case: the vendor IS named, so the mount is not the answer.

quiet.why: AC 3. The Windows global store is not synced by default — the WARN offers it as the alternative.
ARC-04-S02 criterion 8: the word inside a longer name is not a folder boundary.

env.why: Known Folder Move: the enterprise policy redirects Documents into OneDrive and the word OneDrive appears nowhere in the path. %OneDrive% is the only detector there is.
The commercial client sets its own variable.
The variable is set but this path is not under it — a set variable is not a blanket yes.
